documents.title: Office Visit - snoring, sleepiness; diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chief concern: wife's report of snoring.

HPI: 58-year-old long-haul driver here for his summer diabetes visit, fasting. His wife sent him in about his sleep: she says his snoring has gotten loud enough that she has moved to the couch some nights, and that she has watched him stop breathing for stretches before he snorts and starts again. He feels sleepy through the day, worse in the afternoon, and has been pulling over for naps more often on long hauls. Has not had a crash or near-miss. No morning headaches reported. Father had sleep apnea.

Diabetes/BP: taking all five medicines. Home BP 130s/80s.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: BP 134/83, HR 65, RR 14, T 36.5, SpO2 96%. Wt 101.7 kg, BMI 32.1.
Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

Assessment / Plan
1. Loud snoring, witnessed pauses in breathing and daytime sleepiness, in a man with obesity, hypertension and a father with OSA. Referral to pulmonology for sleep evaluation. Advised to pull over and rest whenever drowsy, and not to push through.
2. T2DM - A1c and fasting glucose today. Continue metformin.
3. HTN - 134/83, continue.
4. HLD - lipid panel today.
5. Annual lung CT - order placed for September.
Physical in October.

documents.title: Pulmonology sleep consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY & SLEEP MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/25/2022
Patient: Lamar Bryant, 58-year-old man
Requested by: primary care, for evaluation of snoring and daytime sleepiness

History of present illness: Mr. Bryant has longstanding type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia and is established with endocrinology and cardiology. He comes to us for new sleep symptoms. He is drowsy across the day. His snoring is heavy, and his wife has seen him stop breathing at night, which wakes her. He often wakes with a dry mouth and now and then with a sensation of choking. He has no chest pain, palpitations or leg swelling.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril and atorvastatin; amlodipine 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history is notable for a father with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea; mother with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; paternal uncle with coronary artery disease.
Social history: long-haul truck driver. Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2011. Alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

Examination:
BP 138/86, HR 88, BMI 32.
Oropharynx: enlarged tonsils; posterior pharynx crowded.
Neck circumference 43 cm.
Remainder of the examination unremarkable.

Laboratory (from primary care, 06/28/2022): fasting glucose 146 mg/dL, HbA1c 7.2%, total cholesterol 190, HDL 40, LDL 120, triglycerides 150 mg/dL.

Impression: Symptoms and examination suggest obstructive sleep apnea.

Plan: Home sleep apnea test ordered. Results will be sent to primary care.

reports.text:
HOME SLEEP APNEA TEST — INTERPRETATION
Ordering service: pulmonology / sleep medicine
Indication: snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime sleepiness.
Device: type III portable monitor (airflow, effort belts, oximetry, position). Single night at home.
Recording quality: adequate for interpretation.
Respiratory events: apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 24 events per hour, predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas.
Oximetry: oxygen saturation nadir 84%.
Pulse rate: no sustained abnormality on the oximetry channel.

IMPRESSION: Moderate obstructive sleep apnea (AHI 24 events per hour, oxygen nadir 84%).
reports.conclusion: Moderate obstructive sleep apnea (AHI 24/hour, SpO2 nadir 84%). Results to ordering clinician.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST FOR LUNG CANCER SCREENING (annual)
Clinical history: 58-year-old former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2011.
Technique: Low-dose non-contrast helical CT of the chest.
Comparison: 09/14/2021.
Findings:
No pulmonary nodule or mass. Lungs clear without consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
Central airways patent.
No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Heart normal in size. No pericardial effusion. Normal caliber thoracic aorta.
Limited upper abdomen unremarkable. No aggressive osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Recommend annual low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - trouble swallowing; diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reason: diabetes follow-up; new swallowing problem.

HPI: 59-year-old man, fasting for labs. Over roughly the last five months, swallowing has been getting harder. Solid food and drinks both seem to hang up; he points to the middle of his chest as the spot where food stops. A few times a week food comes back up into his mouth, sometimes well after the meal. He has learned to eat slowly and wash things down with water. No weight loss (weight steady here). No vomiting blood, no black stools, no heartburn to speak of. No pain with swallowing.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Swallowing the pills ok with water.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 130/86, HR 78, RR 14, T 36.2, SpO2 96%. Weight 101.0 kg, BMI 31.6.
Not pale. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses.

Assessment / Plan
1. Progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids with regurgitation, ~5 months. Referral to gastroenterology for evaluation and endoscopy. CBC today. Call sooner if food gets stuck and won't pass, or if he starts losing weight.
2. T2DM: A1c and fasting glucose today. Continue metformin.
3. HTN: 130/86, fine.
4. Lung CT due September - order placed.
5. Eye exam due next month, he has it booked.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date: 08/02/2023
Patient: Lamar Bryant (DOB 02/26/1964)
Referring: primary care, for dysphagia

HPI: 59-year-old man whose history includes type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia and obstructive sleep apnea. Over the past six months swallowing has become steadily more difficult, for both solids and liquids. From time to time undigested food comes back up, and after he eats he feels food lodged behind the middle of his breastbone. He has not lost a meaningful amount of weight and reports no vomiting or change in bowel habit.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin; amlodipine 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history is notable for a father with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea; mother with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; paternal uncle with CAD.
Social: long-haul driver. Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2011. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month.

Exam: Vital signs within normal limits. No pallor. No lymphadenopathy. Cardiovascular examination unremarkable. Abdomen soft and nontender, unremarkable.

Labs (primary care, 07/11/2023): hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, WBC 7,000/uL, fasting glucose 158 mg/dL, HbA1c 7.1%.

Assessment: Progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids with regurgitation.
Plan: Upper endoscopy performed today (see procedure note). Biopsies sent; we will write again with pathology.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy (EGD) with biopsy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
UPPER ENDOSCOPY (EGD) — PROCEDURE NOTE
Date: 08/02/2023
Indication: dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation.
Consent: risks, benefits and alternatives discussed; written consent obtained.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Tolerated well, no complications.
Findings:
- Esophagus: dilated lumen with retained food residue. The lower esophageal sphincter is tight and does not relax with swallowing; the scope passed into the stomach with gentle pressure. Mucosa without mass. Biopsies taken from the esophagus.
- Stomach: normal.
- Duodenum: normal to the second portion.
Impression: dilated esophagus with retained food and a non-relaxing lower esophageal sphincter. Biopsies pending.
Estimated blood loss: minimal.

events.reason: Esophageal biopsy pathology and GI follow-up letter

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: esophagus, biopsies (multiple fragments).
Gross: several tan soft-tissue fragments, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: squamous mucosa with preserved maturation. No dysplasia or malignancy. No increase in intraepithelial eosinophils. No fungal organisms identified.
reports.conclusion: Esophageal biopsies: benign squamous mucosa. Negative for malignancy. No eosinophilic infiltration.

documents.title: Gastroenterology letter: biopsy results
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY — RESULTS LETTER
Date: 08/08/2023
Re: Lamar Bryant (DOB 02/26/1964)
To: primary care

The esophageal biopsies from Mr. Bryant's endoscopy on 08/02/2023 have returned. They show no malignancy and no eosinophilic infiltration.

Taken together with his six months of progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation of undigested food, and the endoscopic findings of a dilated esophagus holding food residue with a lower esophageal sphincter that fails to relax, the diagnosis is achalasia.

I have discussed these results with Mr. Bryant by telephone.

Allergies: NKDA.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST - LUNG CANCER SCREENING
History: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2011. Annual screening.
Technique: low-dose CT chest without contrast.
Comparison: 09/13/2022 and 09/14/2021.
Findings:
Lungs: no nodules. No consolidation or effusion. No pneumothorax.
Mediastinum: the esophagus is dilated along its course, consistent with the patient's known achalasia. No lymphadenopathy. Normal heart size; no pericardial effusion. Thoracic aorta normal caliber.
Upper abdomen: no acute finding on included images.
Osseous structures: no suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Dilated esophagus consistent with known achalasia. Annual LDCT in 12 months.
